[{"node": "menu_content106", "element": "menu_content", "data": {"label": "Recipes", "key": "recipes_menu_content", "id": "recipes_menu_content", "name": "recipes_menu_content"}, "elements": [{"node": "markdown101", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Recipes take ingredients out of stock", "key": "md_recipes_take_ingredients_out_of_stock", "id": "recipes-take-ingredients-out-of-stock", "name": "md_recipes_take_ingredients_out_of_stock", "value": "# Recipes take ingredients out of stock

A **recipe** is what the kitchen uses to make one unit of a dish: 1 bun, 150 g of beef, 30 g of tomato. In Ren the recipe is an ERPNext **BOM**, so it has ERPNext's costing. When dishes are sold, their ingredients leave stock automatically, without Work Orders.

Recipes are optional: an item without one works exactly as before.
"}}, {"node": "markdown102", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Set up a recipe", "key": "md_set_up_a_recipe", "id": "set-up-a-recipe", "name": "md_set_up_a_recipe", "value": "# Set up a recipe

1. Make the dish an item that is **not kept in stock** (*Maintain Stock* off): its ingredients are.
2. Create a **BOM** for the dish with its ingredients and quantities for one unit (Quantity 1), and submit it. Never put the dish itself among its components.
3. In the dish's **Restaurant** tab, pick it in **Recipe (BOM)**, or leave it empty to use the item's default BOM. **Recipe Cost** shows what one unit costs.
4. In the dish's options, make each part a **component** pointing at its ingredient (with its **Portion**), so removing or doubling it changes what leaves stock.
5. Sizes (variants) use their own BOM; a variant without one uses the template's.

Preparations made in batches (house sauce, dough) get their own BOM and are made with a Stock Entry *Manufacture* when the kitchen prepares them; recipes then use them like any ingredient.
"}}, {"node": "markdown103", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "How options change the recipe", "key": "md_how_options_change_the_recipe", "id": "how-options-change-the-recipe", "name": "md_how_options_change_the_recipe", "value": "# How options change the recipe

| The guest asks | Ingredient in the recipe | Ingredient not in the recipe |
|---|---|---|
| As it comes | the recipe's quantity | — |
| NO tomato | none | — |
| LIGHT tomato | half | — |
| EXTRA tomato, or x2 | double | — |
| Add cheese x2 | — | 2 × its Ingredient Qty |
| Salad instead of fries | fries: none | salad: its Portion |
| A dish inside a combo | — | that dish's recipe, with its own changes |
| A component with sizes | — | the size chosen (its recipe, or itself if it's a stock item) |

A combo without a recipe of its own takes out exactly what its components use.
"}}, {"node": "markdown104", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "When stock is updated", "key": "md_when_stock_is_updated", "id": "when-stock-is-updated", "name": "md_when_stock_is_updated", "value": "# When stock is updated

Ren doesn't touch stock on every sale. Paid orders are gathered and their ingredients leave stock with **one Stock Entry *Material Issue* per POS Profile**:

- when a cashier **closes their register**;
- every day, for anything left (registers not closed, or POS without registers).

The entry goes out of the POS Profile's warehouse to the company's *Cost of Goods Sold*. Only POS Profiles with **Update Stock** on take stock out, the same rule as the invoices. If an entry can't be made (for example, not enough stock and negative stock not allowed), the orders stay pending and the error is in the **Error Log**; closing the register is never blocked.

Each paid order shows the entry that counted it in **Ingredients Taken Out**.
"}}, {"node": "markdown105", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Theoretical and actual usage", "key": "md_theoretical_and_actual_usage", "id": "theoretical-and-actual-usage", "name": "md_theoretical_and_actual_usage", "value": "# Theoretical and actual usage

What leaves stock this way is the **theoretical** usage: what the recipes say. Count your stock now and then with a **Stock Reconciliation**: the difference between the count and the theoretical stock is waste, spills, portions served too large or theft.
"}}]}]
